feedback.problem:
Consider the matrices $A$ and $C$ given below. Find $det({A}^{T})-det({C}^{T}).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 18 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 6 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have the following:   

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 18 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 6 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}|=7\cdot 2\cdot (-1)\cdot (-2)=28 \\ det(C) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 5 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|=3\cdot (-1)\cdot 3\cdot (-3)=27\end{aligned}
$$

Also, 

$$
\begin{aligned}det({A}^{T}) & =det(A)=28 \\ det({C}^{T}) & =det(C)=27.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det({A}^{T})-det({C}^{T})=28-27=1.
$$
